3) It is the case of the appellants that on 29.01.2018 the deceased was driving his motorcycle bearing Reg. No.GJ-09-AQ-3254, at that time one Dumper bearing Reg. No.GJ-02-XX-0635, came from opposite side with full speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed with the motorcycle of the deceased due to which the deceased sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.

Therefore,
the appellants had filed MAC Petition seeking compensation, wherein, the learned Tribunal after appreciating the evidence produced on record has allowed the claim petition.

4) Learned Advocate for the appellants - claimants has submitted that the learned Tribunal has erred in not awarding loss of consortium to each appellants in view of Magma General Insurance Co.
Ltd., Vs Nanu Ram Alias Churu Ram & Ors, in Civil Appeal No.9581 of 2018, and New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Smt. Somwati and others, in Civil Appeal No.3093 of 2020.

5) Learned Advocate for the respondent - Insurance Company has opposed the present appeal on the ground that the learned Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence produced on record and awarded the compensation as per the National Insurance NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/736/2026 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/03/2026 undefined Company Ltd. sentences.text: Hence, he has requested to dismiss the present appeal.
6) The appeal is filed on limited ground that the learned Tribunal has not awarded loss of consortium to each appellants hence the appeal is required to be decided in narrow compass.
Perusing the impugned judgment it appears that the learned Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.12,97,520/- out of which Rs.44,000/- was awarded towards loss of consortium.
The claim petition was filed by six claimants - appellants herein but the learned Tribunal has awarded loss of consortium to only one claimant.

Therefore, in view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram, reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 and Janabai Wd/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs M/s ICICI Lambord Insurance Company Ltd., reported in 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 666, the learned Tribunal has committed error in awarding only Rs.44,000/- towards loss of consortium, however, in view of above judgments the appellant no.1 being widow of the deceased is entitled for Rs.48,400/- under the head of spousal consortium, whereas, the appellant nos.2 to 6 being children of the deceased are entitled for Rs.48,400/- each under the head of parental consortium as they lost the care and protection of their father.

7) As discussed above, the appellants - original claimants are entitled to get compensation computed as under:
Heads Awarded by Reassessed by this Court Tribunal Dependency loss Rs.12,20,520/- Rs.12,20,520/-
 Loss of estate Rs.16,500/-

Funeral expenses Rs.16,500/- 
 Loss of consortium Rs.44,000/-

 Total compensation Rs.12,97,520/- 
 incl  amou

8) In view of above, as the Tribunal has awarded total compe of Rs.12,97,520/-, however, as discussed above the appellants are entitled to get additional amount of Rs.8,40,700/- (Rs.15,43,920/- - Rs.12,97,520/-) with proportionate costs and interest as awarded by the learned Tribunal.
9) Hence, present appeal is allowed.
The judgment and award dated 04.11.2023 passed by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Main), Mahesana, in MAC Petition No.63 of 2018 stands modified to the aforesaid extent.
Rest of the judgment and award remains unaltered.

The respondent no.3 - Insurance Company shall deposit the said additional amount of Rs.8,40,700/- along with interest as NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/736/2026 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/03/2026 undefined awarded by the Tribunal, before the Tribunal within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of this order.
Record and proceedings be remitted back to the concerned Tribunal forthwith.

10) The learned Tribunal is directed to recover or deduct the deficit court fees on enhanced amount and thereafter disburse the amount accordingly.
11) Interim application, if any, also stands disposed of.
12) Award to be drawn accordingly.
